text:
Jim Cramer warned that Nvidia *($NVDA)*'s blockbuster earnings may not be enough to win back investors, arguing that Jensen Huang's departure and Anthropic's upcoming IPO are creating new headwinds for the stock.

• *Earnings Aren't Enough:* “The numbers weren't good; they were fabulous. But it doesn't matter,” Cramer said, arguing that investors have effectively voted Nvidia out of their portfolios.
• *Anthropic Competition:* With Anthropic *($ANT)* set to begin trading Thursday, Cramer believes investors have an attractive new way to gain AI exposure, potentially drawing capital away from Nvidia.
• *Leadership Uncertainty:* Despite praising interim CEO Colette Kress, Cramer said investors want permanent leadership and remain concerned about Nvidia's future without Huang.
• *Investor Sentiment:* “People want a company with a permanent CEO, and they want Jensen Huang,” Cramer said. Rather than wait for the board's CEO search, he believes investors “would rather just get some Anthropic.”

TRUMP: SPOKE TO XI ABOUT CHIPS, AI LAST NIGHT

TRUMP: DIDN'T DISCUSS HUANG WITH XI'

TRUMP ON JENSEN HUANG: SOME PEOPLE CAN'T BE REPLACED
TRUMP: COULD SELL BLACKWELLS IN 2, 3 YEARS

TRUMP: INDICATION THAT IRAN WAS LOOKING AT GASES, BIO WEAPONS

TRUMP ON BIOWEAPONS: PEOPLE SHOULDN'T BE PANICKED ABOUT THIS KIND OF THING

Trump called Jensen Huang's removal from Nvidia *($NVDA)* a “tragedy,” describing him as irreplaceable and urging greater protection for America's leading innovators during a Fox News interview from Shenzhen, China.

• *Talks With Xi:* Trump said he did not discuss Huang's situation with Chinese President Xi Jinping, though he may have briefly mentioned it. “It's such a tragedy. He's such a brilliant man.”
• *Nvidia's Board:* Trump acknowledged directors have their own views but argued, “Some people can't be replaced,” describing Huang as a decade ahead of competitors.
• *Blackwell Technology:* Trump claimed Nvidia's Blackwell chip is 10 years ahead of rivals and too technologically complex to copy, contrasting it with widespread product piracy.
• *Protecting Innovators:* “We have to take care of our geniuses,” Trump said, arguing that exceptional talent deserves support despite personal controversies.
• *Elon Musk Comparison:* Trump claimed he helped Musk overcome major difficulties during his first term, crediting that support with helping enable SpaceX's advances in reusable rockets.

Trump said he has not heard allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy and defended allowing Nvidia *($NVDA)* to sell chips to China, suggesting Blackwell exports could be permitted in two to three years.

• *Alice Huang:* “I haven't heard that she was a spy. She was a businesswoman who bought chips,” Trump said, adding that he did not know whether those purchases were legitimate.
• *China Chip Sales:* “We allow them to buy. In fact, encourage. We want to make money,” Trump said, arguing Nvidia should be allowed to sell chips while restricting its most advanced technology.
• *Blackwell Timeline:* Trump suggested he could permit Blackwell sales to China in two or three years if he remained in office, but announced no immediate policy change.

*Trump said there are indications Iran is exploring chemical and biological weapons as the U.S. restricts its nuclear capabilities, responding to questions about a reported Iranian dirty-bomb plot targeting Washington.*

• *Iranian Weapons:* “There is indication that Iran is looking at gases, looking at bio,” Trump said, suggesting Tehran is pursuing alternatives after nuclear restrictions.
• *D.C. Threat:* Asked whether Washington residents should panic, Trump reportedly responded, “I don't think so, no,” adding: “If it does happen, we wipe them out.”
• *Potential Escalation:* Trump said, “We'll see what happens after January 1st,” without specifying a deadline or announcing military action.

Nvidia *($NVDA)* announced two new multibillion-dollar supply-chain commitments in Taiwan, securing additional advanced chip substrates and packaging capacity for future AI platforms.

• *Kinsus (TWSE: 3189) — Over $1B:* Nvidia is providing more than $1B to expand advanced substrate production at Kinsus' Taoyuan facility. Nvidia-dedicated capacity will increase more than 3.5x, with production starting in H2 2027 and further expansion targeted for Q3 2028.
• *SPIL (NYSE: $ASX) — Multibillion-Dollar Deal:* Nvidia signed a new multiyear agreement with Siliconware Precision, a subsidiary of U.S.-listed ASE Technology Holding *($ASX)*, to triple advanced packaging capacity in Taiwan by mid-2029. Funding covers production lines, interposer fabrication, assembly and testing.
• *Long-Term Supply:* Kinsus said the investment aims to secure substrate availability through at least 2030, with additional expansion investments under discussion.
• *What's New:* Both agreements were first disclosed November 17, with additional details November 18. SPIL's packaging expansion is separate from its previously announced optical-engine capacity expansion.

*U.S. equity futures rebounded Wednesday night ahead of Anthropic's historic IPO, led by technology stocks, while Asian markets traded unevenly and cryptocurrencies remained under pressure. Fresh cybersecurity earnings also sparked significant after-hours moves.*

• *U.S. Futures:* Nasdaq-100 rose 0.63% (+170.6) to 27,286.9, S&P 500 gained 0.38% (+27.6) to 7,351.1, and Dow futures advanced 0.34% (+172) to 50,445.
• *Asian Markets:* South Korea's KOSPI fell 1.99% and KOSDAQ lost 1.85%, while Japan's Nikkei slipped 0.41% in the latest supplied snapshot. South Korea opened an hour late for its national college entrance exam.
• *Crypto & Metals:* Bitcoin traded near $62,472 (-2.84%) and Ethereum near $1,768 (-1.94%). Gold rebounded 0.44% to $3,741/oz, while silver gained 0.34% to $45.21.

• *Cybersecurity Rally:* Palo Alto Networks *($PANW)* jumped roughly 9% after hours after reporting $3.44B in quarterly revenue, raising FY2027 guidance to $14.52B–$14.57B and announcing a $4.5B acquisition of AI startup Applied Compute. CrowdStrike *($CRWD)* gained about 5%, Zscaler *($ZS)* 3% and Fortinet *($FTNT)* 2%.
• *Other After-Hours Movers:* Everpure *($P)* gained approximately 3%–4% after beating earnings expectations and raising guidance. Magnera *($MAGN)* rose about 14% following results showing stronger adjusted EBITDA and cash flow. Red Robin *($RRGB)* plunged roughly 17.5% after missing revenue and earnings estimates.

• *Anthropic IPO:* Anthropic *($ANT)* priced its offering at $83 per share, raising approximately $81.3B in the largest IPO on record. Trading begins Thursday, November 19. Cboe expects options trading could begin Monday, November 23, pending readiness.
• *Thursday Catalysts:* Investors await Anthropic's first trading session, weekly jobless claims and earnings from Walmart *($WMT)*, Alibaba *($BABA)* and PDD *($PDD)* before the U.S. open, followed by Gap *($GAP)* and Ross Stores *($ROST)* after the close.

Trump said the U.S. could allow Nvidia *($NVDA)* to sell Blackwell AI chips to China in 2–3 years, once newer processors surpass them. No immediate policy change was announced, Bloomberg reports.

• *Blackwell Timeline:* “In two years or three years, I would, if I were here, I would say, go ahead. You can now sell Blackwells because they'll have something else,” Trump said.
• *Technology Shift:* Trump said Nvidia is already developing Blackwell's successor and suggested the current generation could become obsolete within a year.
• *China Restrictions:* Washington previously permitted older H200 exports but blocked Blackwell sales. “They didn't even sell that many, the 200s, and the 200s are old now,” Trump said.
• *Tighter Controls:* The administration recently expanded restrictions targeting Chinese access to advanced AI chips through overseas data centers.
• *Congressional Action:* Republican Sen. Jim Banks and Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren are advancing the AI Overwatch Act, which would restrict Blackwell exports to China for at least 18 months. The proposal is under negotiation for inclusion in December's defense package.

*Wall Street's $500B Nvidia *($NVDA)* chip-financing initiative has yet to deploy any capital, with its first deal unlikely to close before 2027. The program was designed to help AI customers finance chip purchases, sustain Nvidia's growth and support its valuation, The Wall Street Journal reports.*

• *$500B Agreement:* Apollo *($APO)*, Blackstone *($BX)*, BlackRock *($BLK)*, Brookfield *($BN)*, Goldman Sachs *($GS)* and KKR *($KKR)* signed an August memorandum outlining a fundraising target, not binding capital commitments.
• *Financing Roadblock:* Nvidia offered credit support covering up to 25% of project costs, but lenders increasingly want stronger guarantees. Broadcom *($AVGO)* provided an approximately 85% residual-value guarantee for Anthropic's $35B chip-financing deal and nearly 75% for a separate $63B deal.
• *Huang's Strategy:* Former CEO Jensen Huang pushed the initiative amid concerns over Nvidia's declining valuation multiple. An earlier proposed $250B backstop for an OpenAI data center triggered a 5% stock selloff, prompting Nvidia to halve its initial financial commitment, WSJ reports.
• *Leadership Shift:* Interim CEO Colette Kress is taking a more cautious approach. “We are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees,” she told investors.
• *Neocloud Risk:* Apollo CEO Marc Rowan warned that without Nvidia's financing guarantees, access to capital for many neocloud providers could disappear. Negotiations for the first chip-backed deal remain ongoing, with no closing expected before 2027.
• *Market Implications:* Nvidia's earnings and outlook remain strong, but tighter financing conditions could constrain customers' ability to fund future GPU purchases, even if the broader $500B initiative never fully materializes.

*Trump is weighing renewed joint U.S.-Israeli strikes against Iran as Israel warns of expanding chemical weapons research, while Gulf nations urge restraint over fears of retaliation against regional energy infrastructure, Axios reports.*

• *Military Options:* Trump requested assessments of Iran's likely retaliation, particularly against Gulf oil and gas facilities.
• *Israeli Pressure:* Netanyahu is pushing for swift military action. Mossad chief Roman Gofman met U.S. officials and presented intelligence alleging increased Iranian chemical weapons research and testing.
• *Intelligence Disputes:* U.S. and Israeli officials acknowledge increased Iranian chemical weapons activity but say Tehran currently lacks the capability to launch such attacks. Some U.S. officials questioned Israel's intelligence and its urgency.
• *U.S. Divisions:* Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth favors stronger military action, while Gulf leaders advocate continued economic pressure. Trump said Wednesday, “We'll see what happens after January 1.”
• *Regional Escalation:* Iran has resumed drone attacks on U.S. bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. Maritime tensions in the Strait of Hormuz are also rising.
• *Diplomatic Efforts:* Qatari and Pakistani mediators continue seeking a U.S.-Iran agreement, but recent talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi produced no significant progress. CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper also met Israeli and Saudi officials to coordinate regional security.

*Trump defended AI development at the APEC summit, warning against regulations that could stifle innovation while acknowledging potential risks. He also highlighted falling inflation, U.S. economic priorities in the Pacific and anticipated meetings with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.*

• *AI Regulation:* Trump described AI as overwhelmingly positive but said its potential downsides require careful management. He opposed regulations that would “stifle” AI development, declaring his administration would not allow that to happen.
• *Inflation:* Trump said inflation had fallen more than anticipated over the past three months, without providing specific figures.
• *U.S. Pacific Strategy:* Trump reaffirmed America's commitment to strengthening economic growth, sovereignty, stability, prosperity and peaceful development throughout the region.
• *Global Diplomacy:* Trump said he looks forward to meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

*Wealthy family offices increased their stock allocations to 36.4% in Q3 2026, their largest portfolio holding, while reducing private-market exposure and limiting AI-related risk, according to CNBC's Family Office Portfolio Tracker.*

• *Stock Allocations:* Public equities rose to 36.4% from 35.6% in Q2 and 33.6% in 2024. Public markets now represent 53.1% of portfolios versus 46.8% in alternatives.
• *AI Risk Management:* Technology accounts for 28% of family-office stock portfolios versus 40% of the S&P 500. Financials represent 18%, compared with 11% in the index, providing a potential offset to AI-related volatility.
• *Private Markets Decline:* Alternative allocations fell from 48.5% a year ago to 46.8%. Real estate dropped to 7.2% from 9.4%, hedge funds to 7.5% and private equity to 6.4%. Direct private-company holdings remain the largest alternative allocation at 15.7%.
• *Cash & Bonds:* Cash increased to 8.6%, providing liquidity for potential opportunities, while fixed income rose for a third consecutive quarter to 8.1%.
• *Investor Positioning:* Addepar CEO Eric Poirier said family offices remain invested despite AI bubble concerns: “They're fading the AI trade to some extent, but still staying quite exposed.”
• *Data Scope:* The tracker covers hundreds of family offices managing more than $1.4T in assets. Allocation changes reflect both market performance and investment decisions, not necessarily new stock purchases.
